parts:
Hi, everyone. When I tried to use two response (y and logT below) with missing values in both, if the iteration is small like 1000, I can get the result I want. But if the iteration is bigger like 50000, some parameters show NA in the result. I am wondering if there is any solution for this? Thanks. 

code=nimbleCode({
  for (n in 1:N) {
    for (i in 1:I) {
      logit(prob[n, i]) <- beta[i] + delta[i] * prod(w[n, i])
      y[n, i] ~ dbern(prob[n, i])
      logT[n, i] ~ dnorm(zeta[i] + theta[n], den_epsilon[i])
    }}
  for (n in 1:N) {theta[n] ~ dnorm(0,1)}
  for (i in 1:I) {
    item_parameter[i, 1:3] ~ dmnorm(item_mu[1:3], item_den[1:3, 1:3])
    beta[i] <- item_parameter[i, 1]
    delta[i] <- item_parameter[i, 2]
    zeta[i] <- item_parameter[i, 3]
    den_epsilon[i] ~ dgamma(1, 1)
  }
  item_mu[1] ~ dnorm(0, 1)
  item_mu[2] ~ T(dnorm(0, 1),0,)
  item_mu[3] ~ dnorm(0,1)
  item_den[1:3, 1:3] ~ dwish(R[1:3, 1:3], 3)
})

data <- list(y=y, logT=logT)

monitors=c("beta","delta","zeta"," den_epsilon","y","logT")

No problem, Duoduo.  Thanks for sending the Q matrix.  First, I don't see any NA's in the response (data) value of y:

any(is.na(data$y))
## [1] FALSE

And the same is true of "vec1" and "vec2" also, so I'm not entirely sure what you mean by "only consider observed response in model and skip the NA index".

That said, there's an error or two in your model code.  For one, you can't have declarations using an equal sign, like:

            add=vec1[n]
            index=vec2[add+i]

in your model code.  For deterministic model declarations, you should use the R assignment operator, "<-".

But more important, the BUGS language is declarative, not imperative, meaning each declaration (and each iteration inside a for-loop) must declare a unique node.  So this code:

for (n in 1:1000) {
        for (i in 1:vec1[n+1]) {
            add=vec1[n]
            index=vec2[add+i]

.....
        }}

Results in multiple declarations of "add" and "index", which you can't have.  But, we can easily take care of this by defining the equivalent constants, as:


index <- array(NA, c(1000, max(data$vec1)))

for(n in 1:1000) {
    for(i in 1:max(data$vec1)) {
        index[n,i] <- data$vec2[data$vec1[n] + i]
    }
}


(granted, this is not the most efficient way of doing this operation in R, but it's the most clear).

And then everywhere that "index" is used in these nested loops in your model code, replace it with "index[n,i]"

Also, you'll need to move "vec1" and "Q" to the constants list, and add "index" to the constants list.  Some updated code is below:

#model we fit
code=nimbleCode({
    for (n in 1:1000) {
        for (i in 1:vec1[n+1]) {
for (k in 1:7) {

w[n, index[n,i], k] <- pow(attribute[n, k], Q[index[n,i], k])
            }
            logit_prob[1+(i-1)+vec1[n]] <- beta[index[n,i]] + delta[index[n,i]] * prod(w[n,index[n,i], 1:7])
            prob[1+(i-1)+vec1[n]] <- exp(logit_prob[1+(i-1)+vec1[n]])

y[1+(i-1)+vec1[n]] ~ dbern(prob[1+(i-1)+vec1[n]])
        }}
    for (n in 1:1000) {
        for (k in 1:7) {
            logit(att_prob[n, k]) <- gamma[k] * theta[n] - lambda[k]
            attribute[n, k] ~ dbern(att_prob[n, k])
        }}

            add=vec1[n]

in your model code.  For deterministic model declarations, you should use the R assignment operator, "<-".

    for (n in 1:1000) {
        for (i in 1:vec1[n+1]) {
            add=vec1[n]
            index=vec2[add+i]

And the same is true of "vec1" and "vec2" also, so I'm not entirely sure what you mean by "only consider observed response in model and skip the NA index".

That said, there's an error or two in your model code.  For one, you can't have declarations using an equal sign, like:

            add=vec1[n]
            index=vec2[add+i]

in your model code.  For deterministic model declarations, you should use the R assignment operator, "<-".

But more important, the BUGS language is declarative, not imperative, meaning each declaration (and each iteration inside a for-loop) must declare a unique node.  So this code:

    for (n in 1:1000) {
        for (i in 1:vec1[n+1]) {
            add=vec1[n]
            index=vec2[add+i]
            .....
        }}

Results in multiple declarations of "add" and "index", which you can't have.  But, we can easily take care of this by defining the equivalent constants, as:


index <- array(NA, c(1000, max(data$vec1)))

for(n in 1:1000) {
    for(i in 1:max(data$vec1)) {
        index[n,i] <- data$vec2[data$vec1[n] + i]
    }
}


(granted, this is not the most efficient way of doing this operation in R, but it's the most clear).
